scope: Current implemented DistanceHybridPolicy, reviewed read-only on 2026-10-12. Method notes for slides; experimental results are maintained separately by the coordinating agent.
recommended_title: GPT-guided local distance fields for faster robot control
one_sentence_method: GPT chooses a local goal, predicted constraints and a control mode; a local Dijkstra planner and measured-pose follower execute free-space motion, while GPT retains five-action Direct control for contact-sensitive phases.

pipeline: Task + current external/wrist RGB + measured robot state + retained observable history
Astra medium: choose coarse_field or contact_direct, with a semantic phase
Field branch: compact goal/constraints -> fixed local grid -> Dijkstra cost-to-go -> one bounded path -> measured-pose tracking -> OSC action
Direct branch: five normalized 7D actions, executed unchanged until a new model decision or evaluator termination
After every action: measured feedback; local events can request an earlier model decision

observable_fields: Eight robot-state values: end-effector xyz [m], orientation axis-angle xyz [rad], two finger joint positions
policy_input.history: Keep the latest two live image pairs, previous textual observations and accepted model outputs, and local summaries of completed execution-feedback blocks. Full per-action logs remain on disk. Incomplete blocks are preserved.
policy_input.demonstration_scope: The current client supports an optional one-demo variant. The latest zero-shot collision-free configuration explicitly rejects demonstrations; do not mix these experimental conditions in one results label.

compact_prediction.slide_headline: GPT predicts a compact planning description, not 35,937 distance values
fields: Up to four blocked axis-aligned boxes
Up to four unknown axis-aligned boxes
Optional held-object goal reference and external-image anchors

grid.center: Measured end-effector position at the model response's generation observation

compact_prediction.known_domain: The center stays fixed throughout reuse and local goal revisions. Reuse does not move the cube with the robot or expand the known domain. A new model response creates a newly centered field.
compact_prediction.resolution_caveat: 5 mm is a computational grid spacing, not proven 5 mm visual localization accuracy or collision clearance.

goal_anchoring.held_object_goal: Let r be the visually estimated current bowl-center offset from the end effector, d the desired bowl-center offset from c, and R_cur/R_tar the measured/current and requested end-effector orientations. The effective end-effector goal is g = c + d - R_tar R_cur^T r.
goal_anchoring.purpose: Place the bowl center at the intended location while accounting for a nonzero grasp offset and requested orientation change.
goal_anchoring.assumptions: The offset is model-estimated and assumes a rigid grasp; slip and visual errors remain possible. Raw prediction and effective local goal are logged separately.

legacy_compact_U.definition: U(x) = sqrt(sum_a alpha_a * ((x_a-g_a)/ell)^2) + sum_k beta_k * exp(-||x-r_k||^2/(2*sigma_k^2)), with ell = 0.08 m
legacy_compact_U.variables: x and g are world positions; r_k = c + center_offset_k; sigma_k is radius_m; alpha_a and beta_k are positive model outputs.
legacy_compact_U.units: Dimensionless arbitrary-scale potential because the goal displacement is divided by 0.08 m. It is not an obstacle-surface distance or a shortest-path distance.
legacy_compact_U.current_role: Still expanded for compatibility with GridField and its masks. Current Dijkstra edge costs do not use U or attraction_weights. U values remain included in the cache fingerprint, which does not make them part of the path objective.

current_D.cost_to_go: D(v) = min over valid graph paths v -> goal terminals of [sum of w along the path + any validated terminal-edge cost]
current_D.bellman_view: For nonterminal vertices, D(v) = min_{u in valid neighbors(v)} [w(v,u) + D(u)]. Unreachable or invalid vertices have D=+infinity.
current_D.units: rho is dimensionless and w,D have length units. Diagnostics call them m without repulsors and weighted_m with repulsors. With no repulsors, D is shortest geometric length on the finite valid graph, not exact continuous Euclidean/geodesic distance.
current_D.algorithm: Reverse multi-source Dijkstra from the goal region, storing a successor toward a terminal at each reached vertex.

graph_and_constraints.connectivity: 26 neighbors: axis, face diagonal and body diagonal offsets. Edge lengths are h, sqrt(2)h or sqrt(3)h for h=5 mm.
graph_and_constraints.valid_vertices: Remove blocked and unknown grid vertices, points outside configured workspace, and points inside any continuous blocked/unknown box. Blocked takes precedence when discrete blocked and unknown masks overlap.
graph_and_constraints.valid_edges: Require every active interpolation-stencil corner to be valid, and apply a continuous closed-segment/AABB intersection test. This rejects diagonal corner cuts and thin boxes smaller than the grid spacing.
graph_and_constraints.continuous_path_checks: GridField traverses every crossed interpolation cell, checking all active corner sets, rather than only regularly spaced samples. The actual-start connection, extracted path and tracker lookahead chords also receive continuous box checks.
graph_and_constraints.soft_vs_hard: Gaussian repulsors increase traversal cost but do not create hard collision masks. Blocked and unknown boxes forbid traversal.

goal_region_and_boundary.standalone_default: DistanceFieldPlanner.plan defaults to a 5 mm goal-region radius.
goal_region_and_boundary.actual_current_hybrid: The current _TrackingDistancePlanner adapter divides the requested 5 mm by two: Dijkstra uses a 2.5 mm goal-region radius and _DistanceTracker uses a 2.5 mm endpoint tolerance. The outer measured arrival check is 5 mm position plus 0.05 rad orientation.
goal_region_and_boundary.terminals: Valid vertices inside the goal sphere have zero cost. For a fractional goal or a region containing no grid vertex, valid enclosing-cell corners can connect to the sphere via validated virtual terminal edges. The graph solution is exact for this finite augmented graph, not for all continuous paths into the sphere.
goal_region_and_boundary.actual_start: A measured off-grid start connects to its valid enclosing-cell corners; choose the smallest start-edge cost plus D(vertex). Follow the stored successors.
goal_region_and_boundary.failure_behavior: Explicit hold yields no path. Invalid start or unreachable goal yields no_valid_candidates. Goal outside the original cube or a non-valid goal yields needs_observation; the goal is never silently clipped to the cube boundary. These outcomes request a new model decision, not task completion.

path_extraction.slide_headline: One shortest-path route, not an enumerated trajectory bank
path_extraction.candidate_count: Successful planning returns one extracted CandidateRecord, with candidate_count=1 and valid_count=1. Hold/arrival/failure returns zero candidates. Searching up to 35,937 graph vertices is not generating 35,937 trajectories.
path_extraction.smoothing: Merge collinear consecutive graph edges only. Preserve turns and obstacle/repulsor detours. No arbitrary line-of-sight shortcut, spline fitting or gradient descent is used.
path_extraction.local_horizon: Split straight runs into segments of at most 1 cm and retain at most 10 segments. Geometric path length is therefore at most 10 cm, possibly shorter because of the goal region, short turns or horizon truncation.
path_extraction.cache: Reuse the solved D field while grid, center, field content, masks, goal, tolerance, workspace and repulsors are unchanged. Moving the robot alone only changes start connection/path extraction. Fresh model responses reset cache; changed local goals trigger a new cache key.

path_to_actions.slide_headline: A 10-segment path is tracked from feedback, not executed as ten guaranteed 1 cm moves
path_to_actions.tracking: Project the measured end-effector position onto the remaining polyline with nondecreasing progress; target up to 3 cm farther along it. If the straight chord crosses a predicted invalid region, fall back to earlier vertices/projection. Stop translation if no valid reference exists.
path_to_actions.translation_formula: delta_p = (p_ref-p_measured) * min(1, 0.05/||p_ref-p_measured||); normalized translation action = delta_p / 0.05
path_to_actions.rotation_formula: R_err = R_target R_current^T; take the shortest world-frame axis-angle error, cap its norm at 0.15 rad, and divide by the OSC rotation scale 0.5 rad.
path_to_actions.gripper: +1 closes, -1 opens; field hold repeats the last nonzero gripper intent across both controllers, initially open. Direct zero is executed as zero and does not change remembered nonzero intent.
path_to_actions.cadence: Replan the local path after at most ten executed control actions, or earlier on measured path endpoint arrival, a changed local goal, or a field-refresh event. A short geometric path can still be followed over multiple control ticks until arrival or the ten-action window expires.
path_to_actions.physics: Control frequency is 20 Hz. Requested OSC increments and geometric arc length are not guaranteed realized motion. Waiting for GPT does not advance simulated physics; ten actions correspond to 0.5 s simulated control time, not necessarily wall time or 10 cm actual travel.
path_to_actions.orientation_limitation: Planning is over end-effector xyz only. Orientation is controlled separately toward one target; there is no joint-space or full SE(3) collision planning.

switching_and_model_cadence.routing: At each new accepted model response, GPT chooses coarse_field or contact_direct using permitted visual/state/history inputs. near_target is a model label tied to the selected controller, not a measured contact/proximity predicate.
switching_and_model_cadence.phases: Bowl phases are approach, grasp, transport, align, release, verify and recover. Phase names guide behavior but neither prove grasp nor determine benchmark success. Drawer-task variants add explicit handle phases and use task-specific constraints.
switching_and_model_cadence.direct: Exactly five actions per model response. Local visual feedback observes these actions but does not rewrite them; evaluator success, forbidden collision or external interruption may terminate a partial final chunk.
switching_and_model_cadence.field_initial_interval: 30 actions per model response, unless an observable event requests an earlier refresh.
switching_and_model_cadence.field_reuse: At boundaries 30/60/90, extend by 30 up to 120 total only for approach/transport/align + move, reliable visual tracking, at least five measured motion/error records, accumulated measured motion >1 mm, recent visual error no more than 2 px worse than the start of the retained window, and no active reobservation recovery.
early_events: Measured goal reached (5 mm and 0.05 rad)
Invalid measured start/direction/reference or unreachable local path
Five-action commanded translation >=5 mm but realized movement <=0.5 mm
Alignment calibration unavailable after ten actions
Placement verification or local-goal validity concern
switching_and_model_cadence.missing_anchor_nuance: A missing anchor from the outset disables reliable visual reuse/correction; it does not universally stop every initial approach/transport Field action. The nominal 30-action limit remains unless another event triggers.

optional_local_visual_feedback.method: Track a model-specified moving point and target projection with normalized cross-correlation patches in the fixed external RGB image. Visual-reference kind is end_effector or held_object; both points must refer to the same rigid point's current and desired projection.
optional_local_visual_feedback.fit: In planar align only, use measured XY robot motion and observed pixel displacement to fit a local 2x2 image Jacobian: delta_uv approximately J * delta_xy, via least squares. Proposed correction is J^{-1}(uv_target-uv_moving), norm-capped at 1 cm.
optional_local_visual_feedback.checks: Require at least four samples, two-direction excitation >=3 mm in the smaller singular value, bounded conditioning, residual <=1.25 px, and local height/orientation/gripper consistency. This is not camera calibration or depth reconstruction.
optional_local_visual_feedback.adoption: Only a calibrated correction changes the effective XY goal, preserving its Z and original field center/masks. A >2 mm goal change clears the pending path. The candidate goal must stay in the calibration domain, valid field and workspace.
optional_local_visual_feedback.verification: Five reliable stable visual observations can request a placement_observation_consistent model refresh, never certify benchmark success. If placement evidence is missing, bowl-task code may attempt one validated upward reobservation of at most 2 cm with open gripper, for at most ten ticks; drawer task disables this automatic upward move.
optional_local_visual_feedback.recovery_exception: The explicit vertical reobservation path is a separately labeled local recovery, not a Dijkstra detour: preserve hard masks/workspace, ignore soft repulsors, and prohibit lateral/downward geometric segments.
optional_local_visual_feedback.limitations: Anchor semantics and rigid-grasp assumptions come from the model. Good patch correlation or a fitted Jacobian cannot prove a correct grasp, object support, depth alignment or task success.

distance_field_comparison.quantity: Signed nearest-surface distance, usually with zero on a geometric surface
distance_field_comparison.role: Geometry/clearance representation; not inherently a task goal cost-to-go
distance_field_comparison.current_status: Not implemented here; no reconstructed surface or ground-truth geometry is supplied to the policy

distance_field_comparison.role: Lower-is-better heuristic; not a path-distance guarantee
distance_field_comparison.current_status: Retained as compatibility data, not the current Dijkstra objective

distance_field_comparison.quantity: Nonnegative accumulated weighted path length to a local goal region
distance_field_comparison.role: Route around model-predicted forbidden/unknown regions on a 26-neighbor graph
distance_field_comparison.current_status: Implemented; optimal for the constructed finite augmented graph, not exact continuous geodesics

latest_zero_shot_collision_free_scope.shared_prompt: Explicitly remove demonstration guidance; ask both arms to avoid unintended full-arm, finger and held-bowl contacts, include grasp/payload/rotation extents, treat uncertain space conservatively and reobserve rather than push through obstacles.
latest_zero_shot_collision_free_scope.hybrid_prompt: Ask GPT to put relevant solids in blocked_boxes and uncertain regions in unknown_boxes, visually inflate for held-bowl/finger extent, and avoid empty constraints when an obstacle or required margin intersects the intended local route. This inflation is model-estimated; there is no full-robot geometry oracle.
latest_zero_shot_collision_free_scope.evaluation: A simulator-only monitor inspects collision contacts after each real physics substep and final endpoint. It permits specified finger-bowl grasp and bowl-table/plate support pairs, and scores other monitored robot/bowl-scene contacts as failure. Raw LIBERO success remains separate. This detects and stops after a first collision; it is not predictive collision avoidance.
latest_zero_shot_collision_free_scope.monitor_limits: The monitor excludes robot self/internal contacts, scene-scene-only contacts, positive-distance margins and reset-settling substeps; it checks the settled initial state before policy execution.

mechanisms: Compact GPT outputs avoid emitting all 35,937 scalar values
Local Field control amortizes a model decision over more than Direct's five actions
Cached Dijkstra fields avoid repeated full solves when only the measured start changes
Measured-pose following reduces repeated ineffective fixed-increment commands
Local block feedback summaries reduce retained request text
speed_hypothesis.balanced_message: These mechanisms reduce some model/planning overhead. End-to-end speed also depends on model latency, number of actions, contact-phase difficulty, event-driven refreshes and task success. Fewer GPT calls alone does not prove a faster successful task.
speed_hypothesis.result_rule: Label each dataset by task/layout, one-demo versus zero-shot, controller, success criterion and source revision. Use completion-time comparisons only when both runs meet the same success criterion; do not treat collision failures as successful speedups.

claims_to_avoid: GPT directly produces the current Dijkstra distance values
The compact attraction potential is an SDF or a true obstacle distance
The current planner follows the negative gradient of a learned geodesic field
26-neighbor Dijkstra guarantees the exact continuous shortest path
A 5 mm grid proves 5 mm perception or collision accuracy
Ten path segments mean exactly ten 1 cm realized robot motions
The planner still enumerates the old fixed-length trajectory bank
Every Field response always executes exactly 30 actions
A valid end-effector mask certifies full-arm/payload collision freedom
Local visual verification or GPT phase labels prove LIBERO completion
After-contact monitoring prevents the first physical contact
Single paired trials establish a statistically reliable general speedup
